parameters.description:
Skills from skill_framework_version_id to attach to the Group, each entry a { id, breadcrumb_ids } pair. Must be sent together with skill_framework_version_id and contain at least one skill ,  sending only one of the two keys, or an empty array, attaches nothing and returns a 207 with a framework_params_incomplete error.

Every valid skill is attached; every invalid one is skipped and itemized in the errors array of a 207 response. The Group itself is always created, so read skills back from the response to see what was attached.
parameters.name: framework_skills

schema.description:
Skills from `skill_framework_version_id` to attach to the Group, each entry a `{ id, breadcrumb_ids }` pair. Must be sent together with `skill_framework_version_id` and contain at least one skill ,  sending only one of the two keys, or an empty array, attaches nothing and returns a `207` with a `framework_params_incomplete` error.

Every valid skill is attached; every invalid one is skipped and itemized in the `errors` array of a `207` response. The Group itself is always created, so read `skills` back from the response to see what was attached.

breadcrumb_ids.description:
Which position in the framework this skill is being attached at: the ids of its ancestors, from the root down to its immediate parent. Copy one of the trails from the skill's `breadcrumbs` in the search response, in the same order.

Only omit this, or send `[]`, for a skill that sits at the root of the framework. For a skill that has a parent an empty trail is rejected, and that skill is not attached.

To attach the same skill at two different positions in the framework, send it twice with different `breadcrumb_ids`.

skill_framework.description:
The Skill Framework this Group's skills come from, with the version pinned on the Group nested under it.

`null` when the Group uses free-text `learning_outcomes` instead. Present whenever the Group has a framework version pinned ,  **including a Group that has a framework but no skills attached**, so an object here does not imply that `skills` is non-empty.

`skill_framework.version.id` is the only place a response reports the Group's pinned version id, and it is the value to send back as `skill_framework_version_id` when you write. Retiring a version does not move a Group off it; the version changes only when the Group is explicitly migrated to a newly published one, and that applies retroactively to every credential already issued from the Group. See the [Skills Frameworks](#tag/Skills-Frameworks) endpoints.

skills.description: Framework skills attached to this Group, ordered by name. Empty when the Group uses free-text `learning_outcomes`, and when it has a framework selected but no skills that can be tagged ,  unlike `skill_framework`, this is never `null`.

accredible_new_credential_trigger.description: Runs when new credential is observed in Accredible. Existing records establish the initial baseline. Polling follows your workspace plan; snapshots are limited to 4,000 records.

accredible_new_group_trigger.description: Runs when new group is observed in Accredible. Existing records establish the initial baseline. Polling follows your workspace plan; snapshots are limited to 4,000 records.

accredible_new_or_updated_credential_tri.description: Runs when new or updated credential is observed in Accredible. Existing records establish the initial baseline. Polling follows your workspace plan; snapshots are limited to 4,000 records.

accredible_new_or_updated_group_trigger.description: Runs when new or updated group is observed in Accredible. Existing records establish the initial baseline. Polling follows your workspace plan; snapshots are limited to 4,000 records.
